section.title: Objective and Overview
section.para: In this tutorial, you will learn how to use the GMAT's control flow and targeting mechanisms to maintain a Low-Earth orbit in the presence of atmospheric drag. Use the default spacecraft DryMass of 850 kg, DragArea of 15 square metres, Cd of 2.2, SRPArea of 1 square metre and Cr of 1.8. We will follow the initial low orbit for ten days using Jacchia-Roberts drag. The process used in this script is also useful for generating delta-V estimates for LEO stationkeeping of real-world missions. The basic steps of this tutorial are:

step.para: Create and configure the Resource Tree - configure a spacecraft, impulsive maneuver, propagator, XY plot, and differential corrector.
Create a conditional loop using a While statement , to propagate the mission for 10 days.
Run the mission (we will call it mission's Part 1)and observe its behavior when using no orbit control strategy.

Add Part 2 - a control target sequence nested in an If statement that executes at altitudes below 342 km (where drag is a serious factor) and raise the orbit when the threshold is crossed. The threshold triggers the correction; it is not a guaranteed minimum altitude.
Run the Part 2 mission; observe the behavior of the orbit altitude with the control strategy implemented in step 4.

section.title: Creating and Configuring the Resource Tree
section.para: Here we will configure a model of a LEO spacecraft, a propagator, a maneuver, and an XY plot that we will use to visualize the altitude during the control sequence that we will develop in the next section.

step.para: In the Resource Tree, right-click DefaultSC, select Rename, change the name to LEOsat.
Open the LEOsat dialog box/window (for that, right-click --> Open or double left-click on LEOsat) . Set the value in the EpochFormat combo box to UTCGregorian.
Set the Epoch to 05 Jan 2010 00:00:00.000
Set the state elements to these values: X = -4083.9 , Y = 4691.8 , Z = -2576.7 , VX = -4.252 , VY = -5.509 , VZ = -3.284
Your LEOsat window should now look like as shown below. If not, make changes as needed. Click OK to save and close.
Right-click DefaultProp. Select Rename, and change the name to LEOprop.
Open LEOprop dialog box.
In Drag model group box, set the Atmosphere Model to JacchiaRoberts.
Click Select button to the right of the Point Masses list. Add the Sun and Luna as Point Masses to the right-hand side list. Click OK.
Check the box Use Solar Radiation Pressure
Now your LEOprop dialog window should look like the screen capture below. Click Apply, then Close.

section.title: Creating the DifferentialCorrector and Maneuver
section.para: We will use the default configurations for the maneuver and the differential corrector . Follow these steps:

step.para: In the Resource Tree, locate the Solvers folder; expand it if necessary.
Right-click the Boundary Value Solvers, then Add and select DifferentialCorrector.
Rename the added corrector as DC.

In the Burns folder, add an ImpulsiveBurn named DeltaV. If a DefaultIB is already present, rename it instead. Retain Local coordinates, Earth origin, VNB axes, zero Element1/Element2/Element3 and DecrementMass disabled.

Specify the output: right-click the Output folder, click Add, then XYPlot. Open XYPlot box; click Edit X; replace the item in the right-hand column with A1ModJulian; click OK. Click Edit Y; replace the item in the right-hand column with Altitude; click OK. Your XYPlot box should now look as shown below. Click OK to save it..

section.title: Configuring the Mission Sequence
section.para: We will implement the mission in two parts. In Part 1 we will set a While loop with a propagate sequence, and will configure it to propagate for about 10 days. This will still lack any orbit control strategy. Observe the altitude relative to the 342 km trigger. Later in Part 2 a control sequence will raise the orbit whenever the altitude falls below 342 km. This threshold is altitude, not semimajor axis. Below is an illustration of the Mission Tree after you have completed Part 1. Follow the steps below.

step.para: In the Mission Tree, right-click Propagate1 and select Insert after. Choose While in the command template list. Before Apply, set the optional command name to While1 and the Condition to LEOsat.ElapsedDays < 10. Apply and close the panel. Qt validates the complete mission when Apply is pressed.

Right-click While1 and select Append inside branch. Choose the Propagate template, select LEOprop and LEOsat, check Single step, and name the command Propagate2. Apply and close the panel. Your Mission Tree should now look as shown below.

section.para: Now we will configure the While1 sequence so that the ElapsedDays of LEOsat are limited to 10 days, and configure the Propagate2 command to take a single propagation step.

step.para: Open the Propagate1 command dialog box.
Check Single step in the Propagation group. This removes the stopping condition and disables the inactive stop fields.
The command preview should now be Propagate LEOprop(LEOsat);, with any optional command name preserved.
Your Propagate1 box should now look like the screen below. Click OK to save and close it.
Open the While1 dialog box.
Set the Left-Hand Side to LEOsat.ElapsedDays and the conditional operator to "<" (less-than). Select these explicitly rather than relying on the template defaults.
Change the Right-Hand Side value to 10.0.
Your While1 dialog box should look like the screen below. Click OK to save and close it.

section.para: Verify that Propagate2 also has Single step checked, with LEOprop and LEOsat selected. Both Propagate commands must have no stopping condition.

We are now ready to run the first part of the mission and observe the evolution of the LEOsat altitude. Click Run in the Toolbar. A plot should appear looking similar to the illustration below. Notice that the altitude drops below the allowed value of 342 km. We will address this issue below, in the mission's Part 2, by implementing a relevant control strategy.

Just in case you may want in the future to return to the mission executed in Part 1, this is a good point to save your mission under an appropriate name. In order to avoid confusion, you may want to also save it under the name that reflects its becoming the Part 2 mission.

In Part 2, every time the orbit dips below 342 km, the control strategy that we will set up will perform a Hohmann transfer, increasing the orbit altitude. (We assume that by now you know how to configure a Hohmann transfer in GMAT. (If you want to refresh your knowledge, use the Hohmann Transfer Tutorial.)
In the Mission Tree, let us add the Part 2 mission sequence

step.para: Use Insert after on Propagate2 and choose If. Before Apply, set the condition to LEOsat.Earth.Altitude < 342 and name the command If1. Then Apply and close. The Qt If template includes an empty Else branch; leave Else empty.
Use Insert before on the Else row to insert Target1 in the true branch. Set its solver to DC, SolveMode to Solve and ExitMode to SaveAndContinue before Apply.
Add a Vary statement inside Target1.
Add a Maneuver after Vary1.
Add an Achieve command after Maneuver1
Add a Propagate command after Achieve1
Add a Vary Command after Propagate3
Add a Maneuver after Vary2
Add an Achieve after Maneuver2

section.para: The figure below illustrates how your Mission Tree should now look like. The images illustrate the command settings from the older GUI. In Qt, use the typed command fields and Apply, then Close. Resize a command window or scroll its form when lower fields are hidden.

Let us now configure the commands created above, to perform the Hohmann transfer control sequence. Select DC in Target1, with SolveMode Solve and ExitMode SaveAndContinue. Both Vary and Achieve commands use DC; both Maneuver commands use DeltaV and LEOsat. Vary2 also selects DeltaV.Element1. Keep these two Maneuver commands inside Target1.

step.para: Open the If1 command dialog box
Set the typed condition to LEOsat.Earth.Altitude < 342
Click Apply, then Close to save the condition.
Open the Vary1 Command dialog box .
Select DC and DeltaV.Element1. Set Initial Value to 0.002, Perturbation to 0.0001, Lower to -9.999999e300, Upper to 9.999999e300 and Max Step to 0.0001. Click Apply to save.
Open the Achieve1 Command dialog box.
Edit the Goal value to LEOsat.Earth.SMA.
Change the Value to 6734 and keep Tolerance 0.1. Click Apply, then Close.
Open the Propagate3 command dialog box.
Leave Single step unchecked and change the Stop parameter field to LEOsat.Earth.Apoapsis.
The Qt form disables Stop value for Apoapsis, because this event needs no numeric goal. Your command should contain LEOsat.Earth.Apoapsis as its stopping condition. Click Apply, then Close.
Open the the Vary2 command dialog box.
Open the Achieve2 Command dialog box.
Edit the Goal value to LEOsat.Earth.ECC.
Set Value=0.0005; Tolerance=0.0001. Your dialog box should now look as shown below. Click Apply, then Close.

section.title: Running the Mission
section.para: We are now ready to run our Part 2 mission. Press Run. An XY plot showing the behavior of the spacecraft altitude should appear; in its final form it should look similar to the illustration below. Notice that, with the altitude control sequence now added, the spacecraft initiates an altitude-boosting maneuver every time its altitude dips below the allowed 342 km. Save the completed script. Reopen it to verify the saved spacecraft, force model and command settings. Numerical output depends on the epoch and propagation settings; compare the control response rather than expecting every point to stay above 342 km.
